sources.content: Proposal RSK-212: per-queue concurrency limits for the Ruskvale job scheduler. Today Ruskvale applies one global limit of 64 running jobs, so a burst of report jobs can starve the billing queue. This proposal adds a max_running field to each queue definition in ruskvale.yaml. When a queue reaches its limit, new jobs stay in the pending state and the scheduler checks again every 5 seconds. Queues without the field keep using the global limit. The platform team proposed the change on 2026-03-02.

Scope and rollout. The limit counts only jobs in the running state; retries waiting for backoff do not count. The minimum allowed value is 1 and the maximum is 512; values outside that range fail config validation at startup. Rollout happens behind the feature flag queue_limits, off by default in release 4.6 and on by default in release 4.7. Out of scope: limits per tenant and limits based on CPU or memory use. Metrics will expose a new gauge named ruskvale_queue_running for each queue.

claims.text: Ruskvale's current global limit is 128 running jobs.
The queue_limits flag is on by default in release 4.7.
The max_running value must be at least 1.
A Ruskvale queue that reaches its limit leaves new jobs in the pending state.
Retries waiting for backoff count toward a Ruskvale queue's running limit.
Ruskvale queues that omit max_running fall back to the global limit.
